newsitem.title: USA: Clinton lead in California narrows to 12 points.
newsitem.headline: Clinton lead in California narrows to 12 points.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole in the key state of California stands at 12 points three weeks before the election, according to a poll published on Wednesday.

A poll in the San Francisco Examiner found 49 percent of likely California voters backing Clinton and 37 percent supporting Dole, with 3 percent each for Reform Party candidate Ross Perot and the Green Party's Ralph Nader. Eight percent were undecided.
It said Clinton's lead of 12 points was down four points from a similar poll in September.
The telephone survey of 801 likely voters was conducted from Saturday through Monday by Mason-Dixon Political/Media Research of Washington D.C. The margin of error was 3.5 percentage points.
The Dole camp was buoyed by a poll by the independent Field Institute last week showing Dole had cut Clinton's lead in California -- a crucial state with 54 electoral college votes -- to 10 points.
The New York Times this week quoted senior aides to Dole as saying they had tentatively decided to pour resources into California while pulling back in other important states.

The San Francisco Examiner said the latest poll offered few positive signs for the Republican nominee. It said the poll showed that California voters who view Dole negatively outnumber those who see him favourably and that he lags far behind Clinton among women.

It said Clinton was favoured by voters in every region of the state and led Dole by two to one among independent voters. The Examiner quoted pollster Del Ali as saying the new poll calls into question Dole's reported strategy to concentrate on California in the campaign's final weeks.

Dale Neugebauer, press secretary for Dole's California campaign, asserted that the Examiner poll had oversampled Democrats. Adjusting for this, it was "probably closer to a five-point race," he said. He said California was a winnable state for Dole.
